entities.summary: Robert de Sorbon was a French theologian who played a pivotal role in shaping the spiritual landscape of medieval Europe. Born in the late 13th century, he rose to prominence as the chaplain of Louis IX of France, and his influence extended far beyond his lifetime. In 1253, he founded the Sorbonne college in Paris, which would become a hub for intellectual inquiry and a symbol of the emerging University of Paris. This institution would go on to educate some of the most influential thinkers of the Middle Ages, including the philosopher William of Ockham and the theologian Thomas Aquinas. De Sorbon's legacy extends beyond academia, as his emphasis on theological education and his commitment to the pursuit of knowledge helped shape the intellectual currents of the time. His impact can still be felt today, as the Sorbonne remains a leading center of learning and intellectual inquiry.
